narrative:
The model predicts you have a 92% chance of leaving your job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This high probability means the system sees strong signs that you are likely to depart soon, based on patterns from many similar employees.

The three factors that most strongly shaped this outlook were your overall years of experience, whether you received other job offers, and how long you have been with this organization. Your total experience of 6-10 years was the biggest influence pushing the prediction toward leaving. Among employees the model expected to stay, half had only 1-5 years of total experience, so your longer track record actually worked against you here, as the model associates mid-level experience with higher turnover risk. 

Receiving other job opportunities was the second strongest driver and also pulled the prediction toward leaving. Only 23% of employees predicted to stay had received outside offers, making this a clear signal of potential departure. 

Your 1-5 years in your current role was the third most important factor and similarly increased the likelihood of leaving. This is shorter than the tenure of many who stay, reinforcing the impression that you may not be fully settled.

The organization should discuss your career goals with you openly and explore ways to increase your sense of stability and growth here. You may want to reflect on whether your current path still aligns with what you want long-term. (248 words)
